title: Cat Chirping: What It Means and Why Cats Chirp at Birds, at You, and at Each Other
summary: Why do cats chirp at birds, at you, and at each other? A vet explains what cat chirping means, what triggers it, and when to check with a vet.

A single “mrrp” sound or a quick string of “mrrps” has definitely caught your attention as a cat parent.


In this article, I, Ivana Crnec, DVM, will explain the cat’s intriguing bird-like sound that makes you stop and wonder.


**Content:**


1. What Is Cat Chirping? Meaning of the Chirping Sound
2. Why Do Cats Chirp at Birds (and Other Prey)?
3. Why Is My Cat Chirping at Me? Greetings, Attention & Cat-to-Cat Chirps
4. When Chirping Is Normal and When to Check With a Vet
5. Conclusion


## What Is Cat Chirping? Meaning of the Chirping Sound


[Studies](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/253952939_A_phonetic_pilot_study_of_chirp_chatter_tweet_and_tweedle_in_three_domestic_cats?ref=petcube.com) define the cat chirp as “a voiced short call.” In-depth[research](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7000907/?ref=petcube.com) reveals that it “lasts about 0.15 seconds” and has “a pitch between roughly 220 and 1,190 Hz.”


Basically, it is short, high-pitched, and mimics bird or rodent sounds. For comparison, the standard[feline “meow”](https://petcube.com/blog/chatty-catties-what-a-cats-language-means/) is much longer and more drawn out.


Some cats make a single chirp, while others do it in a string. A longer string of repeated chirps is known as “chirrups.”


## Why Do Cats Chirp at Birds (and Other Prey)?


Cats chirp at birds, insects, and rodents because prey is the number one trigger for chirping. No matter how well-fed and spoiled they are, modern and even fully indoor cats retain their predatory drive.


The chirp is part of the cat’s hunting mode, alongside a low, tense crouch; a fixed stare with wide pupils; forward-pricked ears; and[tail lashing](https://petcube.com/blog/cats-body-language/) .


“When my cats chirp, they do it because they see a bird through the window,” and “mine do it when they see anything that flies: flies, birds, moths etc.” report two[Reddit users](https://www.reddit.com/r/cat/comments/1ax86co/hello_like_five_minutes_ago_my_cat_started/?ref=petcube.com) .


An old theory suggests that chirping is a kill-bite rehearsal, as the fast jaw movement during a chirp mimics the neck bite a cat would use on its prey.


Use the[Petcube App](https://petcube.com/mobile-app/?ref=petcube.com) to track your cat’s behaviors and reveal their chirping triggers. The app also helps you stay on top of your cat’s physical and mental health.


## Why Is My Cat Chirping at Me? Greetings, Attention & Cat-to-Cat Chirps


If your cat is chirping at you, they are either happy to see you and greeting you, or trying to grab your attention (to get food,[playtime](https://petcube.com/blog/pet-projects-diy-cat-puzzle-box/) , or petting).


Cat-to-cat chirps are more complex and most common in mother cats. “Mother cats often use chirps as contact calls to communicate with their kittens,” says Alison Gerken, DVM, in a[PetMD](https://www.petmd.com/cat/general-health/cat-noises?ref=petcube.com) article.


## When Chirping Is Normal and When to Check With a Vet


Chirping is normal in otherwise healthy cats when it’s associated with prey-watching, play, friendly greetings, and attention-seeking.


You should see a veterinarian about chirping if it:


- Starts suddenly (especially in older cats)
- Changes in sound (becomes raspy or strained) or comes with[coughing](https://petcube.com/blog/cat-coughing/) ,[sneezing](https://petcube.com/blog/cat-sneezing/) , or heavy breathing
- Happens alongside[lethargy](https://petcube.com/blog/lethargic-cats/) ,[vomiting](https://petcube.com/blog/cat-vomiting/) , appetite changes, confusion,[hiding](https://petcube.com/blog/why-is-my-cat-hiding/) ,[loss of litter box habits](https://petcube.com/blog/cat-peeing-outside-the-litter-box/) , etc.


## Conclusion


The chirp is a contact call, a form of vocalization that cats use when they’re focused or aroused in a friendly, eager way.


Chirping is perfectly normal in healthy cats. Keep an eye on your cat and pay attention to what the chirp is aimed at to decipher its exact meaning.
